events.title: Death of Leonardo da Vinci
events.description: Leonardo da Vinci, the Italian polymath, painter of the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, died at Clos Lucé near Amboise, France, at age 67, in the service of King Francis I.
events.significance: Leonardo's art, anatomical studies, engineering designs, and notebooks made him the archetype of the Renaissance man and left a lasting influence on art and science.

events.title: Dos de Mayo Uprising in Madrid
events.description: The people of Madrid rose against the occupying French forces of Napoleon Bonaparte, and the revolt was brutally suppressed by Marshal Murat's troops, with reprisals and executions the following day.
events.significance: The uprising sparked the Peninsular War and the Spanish struggle for independence from French rule, and was immortalized in Goya's paintings The Second of May 1808 and The Third of May 1808.

events.title: Fall of Berlin
events.description: Berlin garrison commander General Helmuth Weidling surrendered the city to Soviet forces under Marshal Georgy Zhukov, following the Battle of Berlin and days after Adolf Hitler's suicide.
events.significance: The capture of the German capital effectively ended major fighting in Europe in World War II and led to Germany's unconditional surrender days later.

events.title: Death of Osama bin Laden
events.description: Al-Qaeda founder Osama bin Laden was killed in Abbottabad, Pakistan, by U.S. Navy SEALs during a covert raid (it occurred on May 2 local time, late May 1 in the U.S.).
events.significance: The operation ended a decade-long manhunt for the mastermind of the September 11, 2001 attacks and was a major moment in the war on terror.

events.title: Arrest of Anne Boleyn
events.description: Anne Boleyn, second wife of King Henry VIII of England, was arrested on charges of adultery, incest, and treason and taken to the Tower of London.
events.significance: Her arrest led to her execution on May 19, 1536, and was a pivotal episode in the Tudor dynasty, affecting the succession and the course of the English Reformation, as her daughter later became Elizabeth I.
